question.text:
You are evaluating the financial performance of two retail chains based on their profitability ratios: Chain A: Return on Assets (ROA) = 10%, Return on Equity (ROE) = 15% Chain B: Return on Assets (ROA) = 12%, Return on Equity (ROE) = 18%
Which chain would be more attractive to equity investors based on ROE?

answer.text: Cannot determine from the given data

explanation.text: The Logic: ROE measures the return earned on shareholders' equity. Chain B (18%) beats Chain A (15%), so equity investors — who own the residual claim — should prefer Chain B. The Trap: Picking Chain A inverts the ranking; 'equally attractive' ignores 3 percentage points of ROE; 'cannot determine' wrongly demands leverage data when ROE already summarises the return to equity. Cross-Exam Context: ROE-based stock selection is covered in NISM XV, X-B and XXI-B. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Warn clients that a high ROE from thin equity (high leverage) is fragile — always pair ROE with D/E when pitching a 'high ROE' PMS holding.
